meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 2: Architecture & Protocol Layers (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which responsibilities does the specification assign to the client? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Deciding which tools the model is allowed to see
Attaching the protocol version and capabilities to every request
Storing the user's OAuth refresh tokens for all connected servers

questions.explanation: The architecture page lists exactly A, B, C (plus routing messages and managing subscriptions) for clients. Deciding what the model sees and holding credentials are host concerns.

questions.question: A new hire asks what their MCP server is on the hook for and what the host handles. Which of these are the server's responsibilities? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Deciding which tool the model should call for a given user message
Exposing tools, resources and prompts and describing them
Validating that an access token was issued for this server's own audience
Doing the work behind a call and returning a conformant result or error
Rendering approval dialogs before a tool is executed

questions.explanation: Servers publish and describe their primitives, enforce their own token audience, and execute requests. Choosing a tool is the model's job and showing an approval dialog is the host's; a server never does either.

questions.question: Which observations point at the TRANSPORT layer rather than the data layer? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The SSE response stream drops before the final response arrives
A tools/call returns isError: true after the upstream API times out
The result object is missing its required resultType field
The POST is rejected with 403 because the Origin header is not allowed
The server's stdout contains a line that is not valid JSON

questions.explanation: Framing, HTTP status and stream lifetime are transport concerns. A missing resultType is a data-layer schema violation, and isError: true is a perfectly valid data-layer result reporting a business failure.
